root.name: King's Indian Defense: Pomar System
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e4 d6 5. g3 O-O 6. Bg2 e5 7. Nge2

overview: White combines the g3 fianchetto with the e4-d4-c4 centre, Nge2 and Bg2, then castles. Black plays ...e5 and ...Nc6, aiming at a closed centre after d5 with ...Ne7 and ...f5 kingside play. The game is a manoeuvring King's Indian with less forcing theory.

white_ideas.idea: Close the centre with d5 and expand on the queenside
Castle kingside and play f4 or b4
Use the Bg2 on the long diagonal

black_ideas.idea: Trade in the centre with ...exd4 and ...Nc6 pressure

typical_structures.structure: King's Indian locked centre after d5 with Black pawn on e5

character.notes: Quieter than the main KID but with real chances for both; neither forces matters early.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

soundness.notes: A respectable system for White and sound for Black.

structure.notes: Centre locks after d5 with ...Ne7 (or is exchanged on d4); I read it as closed.

approach.notes: A normal King's Indian line played by strong players.

level.notes: Understanding of plans (f5, c5) matters more than forcing lines.

character.reason: A fianchetto line with less forcing theory than the main KID.

soundness.reason: A normal sound King's Indian line.

structure.reason: After d5 the centre locks, though d4 exchanges are possible.

plans.reason: White uses the extra space and a Bg2 fianchetto, with queenside expansion.
